e-2477.knowledge_point: Using the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation
e-2477.problem:
Find the derivative of $\mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t)$ with respect to $t,$ where $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =(4{t}^{2}+9)\,i-(\frac{1}{t-2})\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k \\ g(t) & =(4t-1)\,i+{e}^{3t}\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k\end{aligned}
$$
e-2477.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

$$
(\mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t))' = \mathbf f'(t) + 2\mathbf g'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivative of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}+9)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{t-2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,k \\  & =8t\,i+\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k, \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t})j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)k \\  & =4\,i+3{e}^{3t}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+2g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+2{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(8t\,i+\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k)+2(4\,i+3{e}^{3t}\,j-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k) \\  & =8(t+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{(t-2)^{2}}+6{e}^{3t})\,j-6\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

e-2478.knowledge_point: Using the Scalar Function Multiple Rule for Differentiation
e-2478.problem: Find $\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)'$ where $[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]$ and $u(t) = t.$
e-2478.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
\big( u(t) \mathbf g(t) \big)' = u'(t) \mathbf{g}(t) + u(t) \mathbf{g}'(t).
$$

Let's find $\mathbf g'(t)$ and $u'(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)g(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)g(t)+u(t){g}^{′}(t) \\  & =1\cdot [\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+t\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t} \\ -1 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -t \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -t \\ 2t{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ -2t \\ (2t+1){e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

e-2479.knowledge_point: Using the Chain Rule for Differentiation
e-2479.problem: Find $(\mathbf f \circ u)'(t),$ if $\mathbf f(u) = \ln u \, \mathbf i + (u^2+5) \, \mathbf j + 4u \, \mathbf k$ and $u(t) =2t^3.$
e-2479.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(\mathbf f \circ u)'(t) = \mathbf{f}'(u(t)) u'(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivative of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{ln}⁡u)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({u}^{2}+5)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(4u)k \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\,i+2u\,j+4\,k, \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})=6{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{u(t)}\,i+2u(t)\,j+4\,k){u}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2{t}^{3}}\,i+2(2{t}^{3})\,j+4\,k)\cdot 6{t}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{t}\,i+24{t}^{5}\,j+24{t}^{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

e-2480.knowledge_point: Using the Product Rules for Differentiation
e-2480.problem:
Find $\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t),$ given the following functions $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\sqrt{t}\,i+{t}^{2}j \\ g(t) & =\frac{1}{t}i+{e}^{t}j\end{aligned}
$$
e-2480.worked_solution:
Using the dot product rule, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f} \cdot \mathbf{g})(t) = \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t))
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}f(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,i+2t\,j, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}g(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})j \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,i+{e}^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\mathbf f \cdot \mathbf g)(t)
&= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{f}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{g}(t) + \mathbf{f}(t) \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\mathbf{g}(t)) \[3pt]
&= \left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} \,\mathbf i +2t \, \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{t} \,  \mathbf i + e^t \,  \mathbf j \right) +
\left(\sqrt{t} \,  \mathbf i + t^2 \,  \mathbf j \right) \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{t^2}  \, \mathbf i + e^t \, \mathbf j  \right) \[3pt]		 
&=\dfrac{1}{2t\sqrt{t}}  +2te^t    +  \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2}\right)    + t^2e^t \[3pt]
&=\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2}  -  \dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{t^2} +2te^t   + t^2e^t  \[3pt]
&= -\dfrac{\sqrt{t}}{2t^2} +\left(2t+t^2\right)e^t.
}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the value of $(2f(t)+5g(t))^{′}$ at $t=1,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3+t} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t-1) \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}2t-3 \\ {t}^{2} \\ (t+1)^{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
By the sum rule, we have 
 

$$
(2f(t)+5g(t))^{′}=2{f}^{′}(t)+5{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,(2\sqrt{3+t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t-1)) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3+t}} \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(t-1) \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-3) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+1)^{2})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2t \\ 2(t+1)\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Hence , we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(2f(1)+5g(1))^{′} & =2{f}^{′}(1)+5{g}^{′}(1) \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3+1}} \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(1-1) \\ 0\end{aligned}]+5[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2(1) \\ 2(1+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+5[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 10 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 10 \\ 20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Find the value of (2f(t)+5g(t))′ at t=1, where f(t)=[23+tcos⁡(t−1)1],g(t)=[2t−3t2(t+1)2]

a

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

By the sum rule, we have (2f(t)+5g(t))′=2f′(t)+5g′(t).

Let's now find the derivatives of each function. f′(t)=[ddt(23+t)ddt(cos⁡(t−1))ddt(1)]=[13+t−sin⁡(t−1)0]g′(t)=[ddt(2t−3)ddt(t2)ddt((t+1)2)]=[22t2(t+1)]

Hence , we get (2f(1)+5g(1))′=2f′(1)+5g′(1)=2[13+1−sin⁡(1−1)0]+5[22(1)2(1+1)]=2[1200]+5[224]=[100]+[101020]=[111020].

content.knowledge_point: Using the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation
content.problem:
Find the value of $(2f(t)+5g(t))^{′}$ at $t=1,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3+t} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t-1) \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}2t-3 \\ {t}^{2} \\ (t+1)^{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
By the sum rule, we have 
 

$$
(2f(t)+5g(t))^{′}=2{f}^{′}(t)+5{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,(2\sqrt{3+t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t-1)) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3+t}} \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(t-1) \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-3) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+1)^{2})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2t \\ 2(t+1)\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Hence , we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(2f(1)+5g(1))^{′} & =2{f}^{′}(1)+5{g}^{′}(1) \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3+1}} \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(1-1) \\ 0\end{aligned}]+5[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2(1) \\ 2(1+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+5[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 10 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 10 \\ 20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Differentiate f(t)+4g(t) with respect to t, given that

f(t)=⟨t,ln⁡t,2⟩g(t)=⟨t,1t,t4⟩

a
⟨1+tt,1t,16t4⟩
b
⟨4t,t−4t2,4t3⟩
c
⟨2t,t2+1t,2t4⟩
d
⟨1+8t2t,t−4t2,16t3⟩
e
⟨4t,1t2,8t⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: By the sum and constant multiple rules, (f+4g)'=f'+4g'. Differentiating each component gives ⟨1/(2√t)+4, 1/t−4/t², 16t³⟩ = ⟨(1+8√t)/(2√t), (t−4)/t², 16t³⟩, matching option d.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+4g(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨\sqrt{t},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨t,\,\frac{1}{t},\,{t}^{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+4g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+4{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,4{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+4g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+4{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩+4⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,4{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩+⟨4,\,-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}},\,16{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+4,\,\frac{1}{t}-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}},\,0+16{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1+8\sqrt{t}}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{t-4}{{t}^{2}},\,16{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 2
?

Differentiate f(t)+4g(t) with respect to t, given that

f(t)=⟨t,ln⁡t,2⟩g(t)=⟨t,1t,t4⟩

a
⟨1+tt,1t,16t4⟩
b
⟨4t,t−4t2,4t3⟩
c
⟨2t,t2+1t,2t4⟩
d
⟨1+8t2t,t−4t2,16t3⟩
e
⟨4t,1t2,8t⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

(f(t)+4g(t))′=f′(t)+4g′(t).

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

f′(t)=⟨ddt(t),ddt(ln⁡t),ddt(2)⟩=⟨12t,1t,0⟩g′(t)=⟨ddt(t),ddt(1t),ddt(t4)⟩=⟨1,−1t2,4t3⟩ Therefore, we obtain: (f(t)+4g(t))′=f′(t)+4g′(t)=⟨12t,1t,0⟩+4⟨1,−1t2,4t3⟩=⟨12t,1t,0⟩+⟨4,−4t2,16t3⟩=⟨12t+4,1t−4t2,0+16t3⟩=⟨1+8t2t,t−4t2,16t3⟩

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option d: f'(t)=⟨1/(2√t),1/t,0⟩ and 4g'(t)=⟨4,−4/t²,16t³⟩. Their sum is ⟨(1+8√t)/(2√t),(t−4)/t²,16t³⟩. The deliberately submitted option c is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Using the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation
content.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+4g(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨\sqrt{t},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨t,\,\frac{1}{t},\,{t}^{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple rule and the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+4g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+4{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,4{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+4g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+4{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩+4⟨1,\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,4{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{1}{t},\,0⟩+⟨4,\,-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}},\,16{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}+4,\,\frac{1}{t}-\frac{4}{{t}^{2}},\,0+16{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1+8\sqrt{t}}{2\sqrt{t}},\,\frac{t-4}{{t}^{2}},\,16{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The original real-valued derivative is undefined at t=−1 because ln(2t) is undefined there. Under the verified repair ln|2t|, f'(−1)=⟨−2,−π,−1⟩ and g'(−1)=⟨−3,−2π,2⟩. Thus 2f'(−1)−g'(−1)=⟨−1,0,−4⟩, exactly option e, the expected website answer.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the value of $(2f(t)-g(t))^{′}$ at $t=-1,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨8\sqrt{3-t},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t)⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨{t}^{2}-t,\,\pi {t}^{2},\,1-{t}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
(2f(t)-g(t))^{′}=2{f}^{′}(t)-{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8\sqrt{3-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{\sqrt{3-t}},\,\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,\frac{1}{t}⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\pi {t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t-1,\,2\pi t,\,-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(2f(-1)-g(-1))^{′} & =2{f}^{′}(-1)-{g}^{′}(-1) \\  & =2⟨-\frac{4}{\sqrt{3-(-1)}},\,\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi ),\,\frac{1}{(-1)}⟩-⟨2(-1)-1,\,2\pi (-1),\,-2(-1)⟩ \\  & =2⟨-2,-\pi ,-1⟩-⟨-3,-2\pi ,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-2\pi ,-2⟩-⟨-3,-2\pi ,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Differentiate f(t)+g(t) with respect to t, given that

f(t)=⟨1−2t,t2,(t−1)2⟩,g(t)=⟨t+1,1−2t,t3⟩

a
 ⟨−1,2t−2,3t2⟩
b
 ⟨−3,2t+1,3t2+2t⟩
c
 ⟨−2,−2t,2t−2⟩
d
⟨−1,2t−2,3t2+2t−2⟩
e
 ⟨−1,2t,t2⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate componentwise: f'(t)=⟨−2,2t,2t−2⟩ and g'(t)=⟨1,−2,3t²⟩. Adding gives (f+g)'=⟨−1,2t−2,3t²+2t−2⟩, matching option d.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+g(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨1-2t,\,{t}^{2},\,(t-1)^{2}⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨t+1,\,1-2t,\,{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
By the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t-1)^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2t,\,2(t-1)⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2,\,3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨-2,\,2t,\,2t-2⟩+⟨1,\,-2,\,3{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,2t-2,\,3{t}^{2}+2t-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Differentiate f(t)+g(t) with respect to t, given that

f(t)=⟨1−2t,t2,(t−1)2⟩,g(t)=⟨t+1,1−2t,t3⟩

a
 ⟨−1,2t−2,3t2⟩
b
 ⟨−3,2t+1,3t2+2t⟩
c
 ⟨−2,−2t,2t−2⟩
d
⟨−1,2t−2,3t2+2t−2⟩
e
 ⟨−1,2t,t2⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

By the sum rule, we have

(f(t)+g(t))′=f′(t)+g′(t).

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

f′(t)=⟨ddt(1−2t),ddt(t2),ddt((t−1)2)⟩=⟨−2,2t,2(t−1)⟩g′(t)=⟨ddt(t+1),ddt(1−2t),ddt(t3)⟩=⟨1,−2,3t2⟩ Therefore, we obtain (f(t)+g(t))′=f′(t)+g′(t)=⟨−2,2t,2t−2⟩+⟨1,−2,3t2⟩=⟨−1,2t−2,3t2+2t−2⟩.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms f'(t)=⟨−2,2t,2t−2⟩ and g'(t)=⟨1,−2,3t²⟩. Their sum is ⟨−1,2t−2,3t²+2t−2⟩, exactly option d. The deliberately submitted option e is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Using the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation
content.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+g(t)$ with respect to $t$, given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨1-2t,\,{t}^{2},\,(t-1)^{2}⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨t+1,\,1-2t,\,{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
By the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t-1)^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2t,\,2(t-1)⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2,\,3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨-2,\,2t,\,2t-2⟩+⟨1,\,-2,\,3{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,2t-2,\,3{t}^{2}+2t-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Differentiate componentwise: f'(t)=⟨0,0,0⟩, g'(t)=⟨−1,0,1⟩, and h'(t)=⟨−2t,0,2t⟩. Their sum is ⟨−2t−1,0,2t+1⟩, matching option c.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+g(t)+h(t)$ with respect to $t$, where

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨-t,\,0,t⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨-{t}^{2},0,{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Using the sum rule, we can write

$$
(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)+{h}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,1⟩ \\ {h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t,\,0,\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)+{h}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩+⟨-1,0,1⟩+⟨-2t,\,0,\,2t⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t-1,\,0,\,2t+1⟩\end{aligned}

Question 5

Differentiate f(t)+g(t)+h(t) with respect to t, where f(t)=⟨−1,0,1⟩g(t)=⟨−t,0,t⟩h(t)=⟨−t2,0,t2⟩

a
⟨t−1,0,t+1⟩
b
⟨−1,0,1⟩
c
⟨−2t−1,0,2t+1⟩
d
⟨−2t,0,2t⟩
e
⟨2t+1,2t+1,2t+1⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the sum rule, we can write (f(t)+g(t)+h(t))′=f′(t)+g′(t)+h′(t)

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

f′(t)=⟨ddt(−1),ddt(0),ddt(1)⟩=⟨0,0,0⟩g′(t)=⟨ddt(−t),ddt(0),ddt(t)⟩=⟨−1,0,1⟩h′(t)=⟨ddt(−t2),ddt(0),ddt(t2)⟩=⟨−2t,0,2t⟩

Therefore, we obtain:

(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))′=f′(t)+g′(t)+h′(t)=⟨0,0,0⟩+⟨−1,0,1⟩+⟨−2t,0,2t⟩=⟨−2t−1,0,2t+1⟩

content.knowledge_point: Using the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation
content.problem:
Differentiate $f(t)+g(t)+h(t)$ with respect to $t$, where

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨-t,\,0,t⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨-{t}^{2},0,{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Using the sum rule, we can write

$$
(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)+{h}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,1⟩ \\ {h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t,\,0,\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t)+h(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)+{h}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩+⟨-1,0,1⟩+⟨-2t,\,0,\,2t⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t-1,\,0,\,2t+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Find (u(t)f(t))′ where f(t)=[et8e−t] and u(t)=t2.

a
[(1−t2)et8t(t+t2)e−t]
b
[3tet−8t−3te−t]
c
[(t2+t3)et4tt3e−t]
d
[(2t+t2)et16t(2t−t2)e−t]
e
[3t3et−16t−t3e−t]
Submit

decision.explanation: Use the product rule: (uf)'=u'f+uf'. Here u'=2t and f'=⟨e^t,0,−e^(−t)⟩, so the derivative is ⟨(2t+t²)e^t,16t,(2t−t²)e^(−t)⟩, matching option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
{(u(t)f(t))}^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})=2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(u(t)f(t))}^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =2t[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 8 \\ {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+{t}^{2}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2t{e}^{t} \\ 16t \\ 2t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{t}^{2}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2t+{t}^{2}){e}^{t} \\ 16t \\ (2t-{t}^{2}){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6

Find (u(t)f(t))′ where f(t)=[et8e−t] and u(t)=t2.

a
[(1−t2)et8t(t+t2)e−t]
b
[3tet−8t−3te−t]
c
[(t2+t3)et4tt3e−t]
d
[(2t+t2)et16t(2t−t2)e−t]
e
[3t3et−16t−t3e−t]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write (u(t)f(t))′=u′(t)f(t)+u(t)f′(t)

Let's find u′(t) and f′(t).

f′(t)=[ddt(et)ddt(8)ddt(e−t)]=[et0−e−t]u′(t)=ddt(t2)=2t

Therefore, we obtain:

(u(t)f(t))′=u′(t)f(t)+u(t)f′(t)=2t[et8e−t]+t2[et0−e−t]=[2tet16t2te−t]+[t2et0−t2e−t]=[(2t+t2)et16t(2t−t2)e−t]

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms the product rule (uf)'=u'f+uf'. With u'=2t and f'=⟨e^t,0,−e^(−t)⟩, this gives ⟨(2t+t²)e^t,16t,(2t−t²)e^(−t)⟩, exactly option d. The deliberately submitted option e is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Using the Scalar Function Multiple Rule for Differentiation
content.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
{(u(t)f(t))}^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})=2t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(u(t)f(t))}^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =2t[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 8 \\ {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+{t}^{2}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2t{e}^{t} \\ 16t \\ 2t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}{e}^{t} \\ 0 \\ -{t}^{2}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2t+{t}^{2}){e}^{t} \\ 16t \\ (2t-{t}^{2}){e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Find (u(t)g(t))′ where g(t)=⟨t,t2,t⟩ and u(t)=2t.

a
 ⟨t2,5t,3t2t⟩
b
 ⟨1,2tt,t⟩
c
 ⟨2,5tt,3t⟩
d
 ⟨1t,5tt,3t⟩
e
 ⟨2t,t,t⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

By the scalar function multiple rule, we have (u(t)g(t))′=u(t)g′(t)+u′(t)g(t).

Let's find u′(t) and g′(t). g′(t)=⟨ddt(t),ddt(t2),ddt(t)⟩=⟨12t,2t,1⟩u′(t)=ddt(2t)=1t

Therefore, we obtain (u(t)g(t))′=u(t)g′(t)+u′(t)g(t)=2t⟨12t,2t,1⟩+1t⟨t,t2,t⟩=⟨1,4tt,2t⟩+⟨1,tt,t⟩=⟨2,5tt,3t⟩.

before.html:
Question 8
?

Find (u(t)f(t))′ where f(t)=[e3te4te5t] and u(t)=t.

a
[3te3t4te4t5te5t]
b
[3e3t4e4t5e5t]
c
[(t2+1)e3t(t2+2)e4t(t2+3)e5t]
d
[(3t+1)e3t(4t+1)e4t(5t+1)e5t]
e
[(t+3)e3t(t+4)e4t(t+5)e5t]
Submit

decision.explanation: The product rule gives (uf)'=u'f+uf'=f+tf'. Since f'=⟨3e^(3t),4e^(4t),5e^(5t)⟩, the result is ⟨(3t+1)e^(3t),(4t+1)e^(4t),(5t+1)e^(5t)⟩, matching option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
{(u(t)f(t))}^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{4t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{5t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{3t} \\ 4{e}^{4t} \\ 5{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(u(t)f(t))}^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =1\cdot [\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} \\ {e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{3t} \\ 4{e}^{4t} \\ 5{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} \\ {e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t{e}^{3t} \\ 4t{e}^{4t} \\ 5t{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(3t+1){e}^{3t} \\ (4t+1){e}^{4t} \\ (5t+1){e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Find (u(t)f(t))′ where f(t)=[e3te4te5t] and u(t)=t.

a
[3te3t4te4t5te5t]
b
[3e3t4e4t5e5t]
c
[(t2+1)e3t(t2+2)e4t(t2+3)e5t]
d
[(3t+1)e3t(4t+1)e4t(5t+1)e5t]
e
[(t+3)e3t(t+4)e4t(t+5)e5t]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write (u(t)f(t))′=u′(t)f(t)+u(t)f′(t)

Let's find u′(t) and f′(t).

f′(t)=[ddt(e3t)ddt(e4t)ddt(e5t)]=[3e3t4e4t5e5t]u′(t)=ddt(t)=1

Therefore, we obtain:

(u(t)f(t))′=u′(t)f(t)+u(t)f′(t)=1⋅[e3te4te5t]+t[3e3t4e4t5e5t]=[e3te4te5t]+[3te3t4te4t5te5t]=[(3t+1)e3t(4t+1)e4t(5t+1)e5t]

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms (uf)'=f+tf', since u=t and u'=1. Componentwise, (te^(kt))'=(1+kt)e^(kt), giving option d for k=3,4,5. Option a omits the f term.

content.knowledge_point: Using the Scalar Function Multiple Rule for Differentiation
content.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
{(u(t)f(t))}^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{4t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{5t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{3t} \\ 4{e}^{4t} \\ 5{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(u(t)f(t))}^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =1\cdot [\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} \\ {e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{3t} \\ 4{e}^{4t} \\ 5{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} \\ {e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t{e}^{3t} \\ 4t{e}^{4t} \\ 5t{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(3t+1){e}^{3t} \\ (4t+1){e}^{4t} \\ (5t+1){e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 9
?

Find (u(t)f(t))′ where f(t)=[4t−13t+25t+6] and u(t)=2t−3.

a
[8t−146t−510t−3]
b
[4t−73t−25t−1]
c
[10t−812t−46t−5]
d
[16t−1412t−520t−3]
e
[12t−1514t−718t−2]
Submit

decision.explanation: Using (uf)'=u'f+uf', with u'=2 and f'=⟨4,3,5⟩, gives 2⟨4t−1,3t+2,5t+6⟩+(2t−3)⟨4,3,5⟩=⟨16t−14,12t−5,20t−3⟩. This matches option d.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
{(u(t)f(t))}^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t+2) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t+6)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-3)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(u(t)f(t))}^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}4t-1 \\ 3t+2 \\ 5t+6\end{aligned}]+(2t-3)[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8t-2 \\ 6t+4 \\ 10t+12\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8t-12 \\ 6t-9 \\ 10t-15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16t-14 \\ 12t-5 \\ 20t-3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Find (u(t)f(t))′ where f(t)=[4t−13t+25t+6] and u(t)=2t−3.

a
[8t−146t−510t−3]
b
[4t−73t−25t−1]
c
[10t−812t−46t−5]
d
[16t−1412t−520t−3]
e
[12t−1514t−718t−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write (u(t)f(t))′=u′(t)f(t)+u(t)f′(t)

Let's find u′(t) and f′(t).

f′(t)=[ddt(4t−1)ddt(3t+2)ddt(5t+6)]=[435]u′(t)=ddt(2t−3)=2

Therefore, we obtain:

(u(t)f(t))′=u′(t)f(t)+u(t)f′(t)=2[4t−13t+25t+6]+(2t−3)[435]=[8t−26t+410t+12]+[8t−126t−910t−15]=[16t−1412t−520t−3]

content.knowledge_point: Using the Scalar Function Multiple Rule for Differentiation
content.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
{(u(t)f(t))}^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t+2) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t+6)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-3)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(u(t)f(t))}^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}4t-1 \\ 3t+2 \\ 5t+6\end{aligned}]+(2t-3)[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8t-2 \\ 6t+4 \\ 10t+12\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8t-12 \\ 6t-9 \\ 10t-15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16t-14 \\ 12t-5 \\ 20t-3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 10
?

Find (u(t)f(t))′ where f(t)=[tt2t3] and u(t)=ln⁡t.

a
[1t+ln⁡t2t2+2tln⁡t3t3+3t2ln⁡t]
b
[ln⁡t3tln⁡t4t2ln⁡t]
c
[1+ln⁡tt+2tln⁡tt2+3t2ln⁡t]
d
[t+ln⁡tt2+2tln⁡tt3+3t2ln⁡t]
e
[t+1tt2+2t3+3t]
Submit

decision.explanation: Use (uf)'=u'f+uf'. Since u'=1/t and f'=⟨1,2t,3t²⟩, the derivative is ⟨1+ln(t),t+2t ln(t),t²+3t² ln(t)⟩, matching option c.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)f(t))^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2t \\ 3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)=\frac{1}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$

$$

after.html:
Question 10
?

Find (u(t)f(t))′ where f(t)=[tt2t3] and u(t)=ln⁡t.

a
[1t+ln⁡t2t2+2tln⁡t3t3+3t2ln⁡t]
b
[ln⁡t3tln⁡t4t2ln⁡t]
c
[1+ln⁡tt+2tln⁡tt2+3t2ln⁡t]
d
[t+ln⁡tt2+2tln⁡tt3+3t2ln⁡t]
e
[t+1tt2+2t3+3t]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write (u(t)f(t))′=u′(t)f(t)+u(t)f′(t)

Let's find u′(t) and f′(t).

f′(t)=[ddt(t)ddt(t2)ddt(t3)]=[12t3t2]u′(t)=ddt(ln⁡t)=1t

Therefore, we obtain:

(u(t)f(t))′=u′(t)f(t)+u(t)f′(t)=1t[tt2t3]+ln⁡t[12t3t2]=[1tt2]+[ln⁡t2tln⁡t3t2ln⁡t]=[1+ln⁡tt+2tln⁡tt2+3t2ln⁡t]

content.knowledge_point: Using the Scalar Function Multiple Rule for Differentiation
content.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)f(t))^{′}={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2t \\ 3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)=\frac{1}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′} & ={u}^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t){f}^{′}(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{t}[\begin{aligned}t \\ {t}^{2} \\ {t}^{3}\end{aligned}]+\operatorname{ln}⁡t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2t \\ 3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ t \\ {t}^{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ 2t\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ 3{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ t+2t\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ {t}^{2}+3{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11

If f(u)=[2uu23] and u(t)=2t+2, then (f∘u)′(t)=

a
[48t0]
b
[44t+40]
c
[24t+40]
d
[48t+80]
e
[22t0]
Submit

decision.explanation: By the chain rule, (f∘u)'(t)=f'(u(t))u'(t). Since f'(u)=⟨2,2u,0⟩ and u'(t)=2, the result is ⟨4,4(2t+2),0⟩=⟨4,8t+8,0⟩, matching option d.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we can write

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(2u) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\,({u}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(3)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2u \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+2)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & =f′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2u(t) \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {u}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2(2t+2) \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot 2 \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8t+8 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11

If f(u)=[2uu23] and u(t)=2t+2, then (f∘u)′(t)=

a
[48t0]
b
[44t+40]
c
[24t+40]
d
[48t+80]
e
[22t0]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the chain rule, we can write (f∘u)′(t)=f′(u(t))u′(t)

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

f′(u)=[ddu(2u)ddu(u2)ddu(3)]=[22u0]u′(t)=ddt(2t+2)=2 Therefore, we obtain:

(f∘u)′(t)=f′(u(t))u′(t)=[22u(t)0]⋅u′(t)=[22(2t+2)0]⋅2=[48t+80]

content.knowledge_point: Using the Chain Rule for Differentiation
content.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we can write

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(2u) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\,({u}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(3)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2u \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+2)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & =f′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2u(t) \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {u}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2(2t+2) \\ 0\end{aligned}]\cdot 2 \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8t+8 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: By the chain rule, (f∘u)'=f'(u(t))u'(t). Here f'(u)=e^(u+1)i+2e^(2u)j and u'=4t; the constant k component differentiates to zero. Substituting u=2t² gives 4te^(2t²+1)i+8te^(4t²)j, matching option b.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)=f′(u(t))u′(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({e}^{u+1})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({e}^{2u})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\frac{1}{e}\,k \\  & ={e}^{u+1}\,i+2{e}^{2u}\,j+0\,k \\  & ={e}^{u+1}\,i+2{e}^{2t}\,j \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2})=4t\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & =f′(u(t))u′(t) \\ (f∘u)^{′}(t) & =({e}^{2{t}^{2}+1}\,i+2{e}^{4{t}^{2}}\,j)4t \\  & =4t{e}^{2{t}^{2}+1}\,i+8t{e}^{4{t}^{2}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)=f′(u(t))u′(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(u) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({e}^{u+1})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}({e}^{2u})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\frac{1}{e}\,k \\  & ={e}^{u+1}\,i+2{e}^{2u}\,j+0\,k \\  & ={e}^{u+1}\,i+2{e}^{2t}\,j \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2})=4t\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f∘u)^{′}(t) & =f′(u(t))u′(t) \\ (f∘u)^{′}(t) & =({e}^{2{t}^{2}+1}\,i+2{e}^{4{t}^{2}}\,j)4t \\  & =4t{e}^{2{t}^{2}+1}\,i+8t{e}^{4{t}^{2}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(g∘u)^{′}(t)=g′(u(t))u′(t)
$$

Now, let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(u) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\operatorname{ln}⁡u,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}0,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\frac{1}{u})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{u},\,0,\,-\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}⟩ \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t})=2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(g∘u)^{′}(t) & =g′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{u(t)},\,0,\,-\frac{1}{{u}^{2}(t)}⟩{u}^{′}(t) \\  & =2{e}^{2t}⟨\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}},\,0,\,-\frac{1}{({e}^{2t})^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2{e}^{2t}}{{e}^{2t}},\,0,\,-\frac{2{e}^{2t}}{{e}^{4t}}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,-2{e}^{-2t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

If g(u)=⟨ln⁡u,0,1u⟩ and u(t)=e2t, then (g∘u)′(t)=

a
⟨e−2t,0,e−4t⟩
b
⟨e−2t,0,−e−4t⟩
c
⟨2,0,−2e2t⟩
d
⟨2,0,−2e−2t⟩
e
⟨2,0,2e2t⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

By the chain rule, we have (g∘u)′(t)=g′(u(t))u′(t)

Now, let's find the derivatives of each function: g′(u)=⟨dduln⁡u,ddu0,ddu(1u)⟩=⟨1u,0,−1u2⟩u′(t)=ddt(e2t)=2e2t Therefore, we obtain:

(g∘u)′(t)=g′(u(t))u′(t)=⟨1u(t),0,−1u2(t)⟩u′(t)=2e2t⟨1e2t,0,−1(e2t)2⟩=⟨2e2te2t,0,−2e2te4t⟩=⟨2,0,−2e−2t⟩

content.knowledge_point: Using the Chain Rule for Differentiation
content.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(g∘u)^{′}(t)=g′(u(t))u′(t)
$$

Now, let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(u) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\operatorname{ln}⁡u,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}0,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\frac{1}{u})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{u},\,0,\,-\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}⟩ \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t})=2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(g∘u)^{′}(t) & =g′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{u(t)},\,0,\,-\frac{1}{{u}^{2}(t)}⟩{u}^{′}(t) \\  & =2{e}^{2t}⟨\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}},\,0,\,-\frac{1}{({e}^{2t})^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2{e}^{2t}}{{e}^{2t}},\,0,\,-\frac{2{e}^{2t}}{{e}^{4t}}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,-2{e}^{-2t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

If g(u)=⟨1u,ln⁡(u+1),1⟩ and u(t)=1t, then (g∘u)′(t)=

a
 ⟨1t,−1t+t2,0⟩
b
 ⟨1,−1t+t2,0⟩
c
 ⟨1,−t1+t2,0⟩
d
 ⟨−1,−t2+t2,0⟩
e
 ⟨−1t2,−t21+t2,0⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Substitution gives g(u(t))=⟨t,ln(1/t+1),1⟩. Its derivative is ⟨1,(−1/t²)/(1/t+1),0⟩=⟨1,−1/(t+t²),0⟩, matching option b.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(g∘u)^{′}(t)=g′(u(t))u′(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(u) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\frac{1}{u}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(u+1)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{u}^{2}},\,\frac{1}{u+1},\,0⟩ \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})=-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(g∘u)^{′}(t) & =g′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{(u(t))^{2}},\,\frac{1}{u(t)+1},\,0⟩\cdot {u}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨-{t}^{2},\,\frac{t}{1+t},\,0⟩\cdot (-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}) \\  & =⟨1,-\frac{1}{t+{t}^{2}},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

If g(u)=⟨1u,ln⁡(u+1),1⟩ and u(t)=1t, then (g∘u)′(t)=

a
 ⟨1t,−1t+t2,0⟩
b
 ⟨1,−1t+t2,0⟩
c
 ⟨1,−t1+t2,0⟩
d
 ⟨−1,−t2+t2,0⟩
e
 ⟨−1t2,−t21+t2,0⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

By the chain rule, we have (g∘u)′(t)=g′(u(t))u′(t).

Now, let's find the derivatives of each function: g′(u)=⟨ddu(1u),ddu(ln⁡(u+1)),ddu(1)⟩=⟨−1u2,1u+1,0⟩u′(t)=ddt(1t)=−1t2 Therefore, we obtain

(g∘u)′(t)=g′(u(t))u′(t)=⟨−1(u(t))2,1u(t)+1,0⟩⋅u′(t)=⟨−t2,t1+t,0⟩⋅(−1t2)=⟨1,−1t+t2,0⟩.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms the chain rule: g'(u)=⟨−1/u²,1/(u+1),0⟩ and u'=−1/t². Substituting u=1/t and multiplying gives ⟨1,−1/(t+t²),0⟩, exactly option b. The deliberately submitted option c is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Using the Chain Rule for Differentiation
content.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(g∘u)^{′}(t)=g′(u(t))u′(t).
$$

Now, let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(u) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\frac{1}{u}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(u+1)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{u}^{2}},\,\frac{1}{u+1},\,0⟩ \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})=-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(g∘u)^{′}(t) & =g′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{(u(t))^{2}},\,\frac{1}{u(t)+1},\,0⟩\cdot {u}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨-{t}^{2},\,\frac{t}{1+t},\,0⟩\cdot (-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}) \\  & =⟨1,-\frac{1}{t+{t}^{2}},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: By the chain rule, (g∘u)'(t)=g'(u(t))u'(t). Since g'(u)=⟨1/u,0,2u⟩ and u'(t)=1/t, substituting u=ln(t) gives ⟨1/(t ln(t)),0,2ln(t)/t⟩, matching option a.

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(u) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\operatorname{ln}⁡u \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\,\,5\,\, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\,\,{u}^{2}\,\,\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{u} \\ 0 \\ 2u\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)=\frac{1}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(g∘u)^{′}(t) & =g′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{u(t)} \\ 0 \\ 2u(t)\end{aligned}]{u}^{′}(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{t}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡t} \\ 0 \\ 2\operatorname{ln}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t\operatorname{ln}⁡t} \\ 0 \\ \frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

If g(u)=[ln⁡u5u2] and u(t)=ln⁡t, then (g∘u)′(t)=

a
[1tln⁡t02ln⁡tt]
b
[u52u]
c
[1u02u]
d
[1ln⁡t02ln⁡t]
e
[1ln⁡t02ln⁡tt]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

By the chain rule, we have (f∘u)′(t)=f′(u(t))u′(t).

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

g′(u)=[dduln⁡uddu5dduu2]=[1u02u]u′(t)=ddt(ln⁡t)=1t Therefore, we obtain (g∘u)′(t)=g′(u(t))u′(t)=[1u(t)02u(t)]u′(t)=1t[1ln⁡t02ln⁡t]=[1tln⁡t02ln⁡tt]

content.knowledge_point: Using the Chain Rule for Differentiation
content.worked_solution:
By the chain rule, we have 

$$
(f∘u)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(u(t)){u}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(u) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\operatorname{ln}⁡u \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\,\,5\,\, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}u}\,\,{u}^{2}\,\,\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{u} \\ 0 \\ 2u\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)=\frac{1}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(g∘u)^{′}(t) & =g′(u(t))u′(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{u(t)} \\ 0 \\ 2u(t)\end{aligned}]{u}^{′}(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{t}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡t} \\ 0 \\ 2\operatorname{ln}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t\operatorname{ln}⁡t} \\ 0 \\ \frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 16
?

Find (u(t)g(t))′ where g(t)=⟨t,t2,2t3⟩ and u(t)=t3.

a
 ⟨2t,5t3,9t4⟩
b
 ⟨4t3,5t2,9t4⟩
c
 ⟨t4,t3,t2⟩
d
⟨4t3,5t4,12t5⟩
e
 ⟨2t,5t4,3t5⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Multiplying first gives u(t)g(t)=⟨t⁴,t⁵,2t⁶⟩. Differentiating componentwise yields ⟨4t³,5t⁴,12t⁵⟩, matching option d.

Question 16
?

Find (u(t)g(t))′ where g(t)=⟨t,t2,2t3⟩ and u(t)=t3.

a
 ⟨2t,5t3,9t4⟩
b
 ⟨4t3,5t2,9t4⟩
c
 ⟨t4,t3,t2⟩
d
⟨4t3,5t4,12t5⟩
e
 ⟨2t,5t4,3t5⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

By the scalar function multiple rule, we have (ug(t))′=u(t)g′(t)+u′(t)g(t).

Let's find the u′(t) and g′(t). g′(t)=⟨ddt(t),ddt(t2),ddt(2t3)⟩=⟨1,2t,6t2⟩u′(t)=ddt(t3)=3t2 Therefore, we obtain (u(t)g(t))′=u(t)g′(t)+u′(t)g(t)=t3⟨1,2t,6t2⟩+3t2⟨t,t2,2t3⟩=⟨t3,2t4,6t5⟩+⟨3t3,3t4,6t5⟩=⟨4t3,5t4,12t5⟩.

Question 17

Find (f⋅g)′(t), given that f(t)=20ti−2tj+(2+5t)kg(t)=t3i+tj+(t2+t)k

a
60t3+7t2+10t+2
b
80t3+6t2+10t+2
c
80t3+11t2+12t+2
d
80t3+15t2+10t+2
e
60t3+15t2+14t+2
Submit

decision.explanation: The dot product is 20t⁴−2t²+(2+5t)(t²+t)=20t⁴+5t³+5t²+2t. Differentiating gives 80t³+15t²+10t+2, matching option d.

after.name: Question 17
after.worked_solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\cdot g)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot {g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(20t)\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+5t)\,k \\  & =20\,i-2\,j+5\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+t)\,k \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j+(2t+1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdot g)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot {g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(20\,i-2\,j+5\,k)\cdot ({t}^{3}\,i+t\,j+({t}^{2}+t)\,k)+(20t\,i-2t\,j+(2+5t)\,k)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j+(2t+1)\,k) \\  & =(20{t}^{3}-2t+5({t}^{2}+t))+(60{t}^{3}-2t+(2+5t)(2t+1)) \\  & =80{t}^{3}+15{t}^{2}+10t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Question 17
?

Find (f⋅g)′(t), given that f(t)=20ti−2tj+(2+5t)kg(t)=t3i+tj+(t2+t)k

a
60t3+7t2+10t+2
b
80t3+6t2+10t+2
c
80t3+11t2+12t+2
d
80t3+15t2+10t+2
e
60t3+15t2+14t+2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Using the dot product rule, we can write:

(f⋅g)′(t)=f′(t)⋅g(t)+f(t)⋅g′(t)

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

f′(t)=ddt(20t)i−ddt(2t)j+ddt(2+5t)k=20i−2j+5kg′(t)=ddt(t3)i+ddt(t)j+ddt(t2+t)k=3t2i+j+(2t+1)k

Therefore, we obtain:

(f⋅g)′(t)=f′(t)⋅g(t)+f(t)⋅g′(t)=(20i−2j+5k)⋅(t3i+tj+(t2+t)k)+(20ti−2tj+(2+5t)k)⋅(3t2i+j+(2t+1)k)=(20t3−2t+5(t2+t))+(60t3−2t+(2+5t)(2t+1))=80t3+15t2+10t+2

verification.explanation: The dot product rule gives (20t³−2t+5(t²+t))+(60t³−2t+(2+5t)(2t+1))=80t³+15t²+10t+2. This confirms the revealed solution and option d; the deliberately submitted option e is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Using the Product Rules for Differentiation
content.worked_solution:
Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\cdot g)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot {g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(20t)\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2+5t)\,k \\  & =20\,i-2\,j+5\,k \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+t)\,k \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j+(2t+1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\cdot g)^{′}(t) & ={f}^{′}(t)\cdot g(t)+f(t)\cdot {g}^{′}(t) \\  & =(20\,i-2\,j+5\,k)\cdot ({t}^{3}\,i+t\,j+({t}^{2}+t)\,k)+(20t\,i-2t\,j+(2+5t)\,k)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j+(2t+1)\,k) \\  & =(20{t}^{3}-2t+5({t}^{2}+t))+(60{t}^{3}-2t+(2+5t)(2t+1)) \\  & =80{t}^{3}+15{t}^{2}+10t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Question 18
?

Find (v(t)f(t))′ given that f(t)=⟨ln⁡t,t2,t⟩ and v(t)=2t.

a
 2⟨ln⁡t,3t2,t⟩
b
 ⟨ln⁡t+1,t,3t⟩
c
 ⟨ln⁡t,3t2,t2⟩
d
 2⟨ln⁡t+1,3t,t2⟩
e
 2⟨ln⁡t+1,3t2,2t⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Using the product rule, (vf)'=v'f+vf'=2⟨ln(t),t²,t⟩+2t⟨1/t,2t,1⟩=2⟨ln(t)+1,3t²,2t⟩, matching option e.

after.name: Question 18
after.worked_solution:
By the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
(v(t)f(t))^{′}=v(t){f}^{′}(t)+{v}^{′}(t)f(t).
$$

Let's find ${v}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,2t,\,1⟩ \\ {v}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(v(t)f(t))^{′} & =v(t){f}^{′}(t)+{v}^{′}(t)f(t) \\  & =2t⟨\frac{1}{t},\,2t,\,1⟩+2⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,{t}^{2},\,t⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,4{t}^{2},\,2t⟩+⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2{t}^{2},\,2t⟩ \\  & =2⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t+1,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Find (v(t)f(t))′ given that f(t)=⟨ln⁡t,t2,t⟩ and v(t)=2t.

a
 2⟨ln⁡t,3t2,t⟩
b
 ⟨ln⁡t+1,t,3t⟩
c
 ⟨ln⁡t,3t2,t2⟩
d
 2⟨ln⁡t+1,3t,t2⟩
e
 2⟨ln⁡t+1,3t2,2t⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

By the scalar function multiple rule, we have (v(t)f(t))′=v(t)f′(t)+v′(t)f(t).

Let's find v′(t) and f′(t). f′(t)=⟨ddt(ln⁡t),ddt(t2),ddt(t)⟩=⟨1t,2t,1⟩v′(t)=ddt(2t)=2

Therefore, we obtain (v(t)f(t))′=v(t)f′(t)+v′(t)f(t)=2t⟨1t,2t,1⟩+2⟨ln⁡t,t2,t⟩=⟨2,4t2,2t⟩+⟨2ln⁡t,2t2,2t⟩=2⟨ln⁡t+1,3t2,2t⟩.

By the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
(v(t)f(t))^{′}=v(t){f}^{′}(t)+{v}^{′}(t)f(t).
$$

Let's find ${v}^{′}(t)$ and ${f}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,2t,\,1⟩ \\ {v}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(v(t)f(t))^{′} & =v(t){f}^{′}(t)+{v}^{′}(t)f(t) \\  & =2t⟨\frac{1}{t},\,2t,\,1⟩+2⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,{t}^{2},\,t⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,4{t}^{2},\,2t⟩+⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2{t}^{2},\,2t⟩ \\  & =2⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t+1,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

a
⟨t6−5,4t5+2t,4t3−10t⟩

 ⟨5t6,t5+4t2,4t3⟩
c
 ⟨7t6,6t5−5,4t3+2t⟩
d
 ⟨−7t6+5,6t5−2t,4t3−10t⟩
e
⟨2t6+1,4t5,t3−5t⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Compute f×g=⟨5t−t⁷,t⁶−t²,t⁴−5t²⟩. Differentiating componentwise gives ⟨5−7t⁶,6t⁵−2t,4t³−10t⟩, matching option d.

after.name: Question 19
after.worked_solution:
Using the cross product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\times g)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\times g(t)+f(t)\times {g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,4{t}^{3}⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,3{t}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t)\times g(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{2} & {t}^{3} & t\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{3} & t\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{2} & t\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ {t}^{2} & {t}^{3}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =⟨-4{t}^{6},\,4{t}^{5}-t,\,{t}^{3}⟩, \\ f(t)\times {g}^{′}(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ t & 5 & {t}^{4} \\ 2t & 3{t}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & {t}^{4} \\ 3{t}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}t & {t}^{4} \\ 2t & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}t & 5 \\ 2t & 3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =⟨5-3{t}^{6},\,2{t}^{5}-t,\,3{t}^{3}-10t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\times g)^{′}(t) & =⟨-4{t}^{6},\,4{t}^{5}-t,\,{t}^{3}⟩+⟨5-3{t}^{6},\,2{t}^{5}-t,\,3{t}^{3}-10t⟩ \\  & =⟨-7{t}^{6}+5,\,6{t}^{5}-2t,\,4{t}^{3}-10t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Find (f×g)′(t) given that f(t)=⟨t,5,t4⟩,g(t)=⟨t2,t3,t⟩.

a
⟨t6−5,4t5+2t,4t3−10t⟩
b
 ⟨5t6,t5+4t2,4t3⟩
c
 ⟨7t6,6t5−5,4t3+2t⟩
d
 ⟨−7t6+5,6t5−2t,4t3−10t⟩
e
⟨2t6+1,4t5,t3−5t⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Using the cross product rule, we can write: (f×g)′(t)=f′(t)×g(t)+f(t)×g′(t)

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

f′(t)=⟨ddt(t),ddt(5),ddt(t4)⟩=⟨1,0,4t3⟩g′(t)=⟨ddt(t2),ddt(t3),ddt(t)⟩=⟨2t,3t2,1⟩

Therefore, we obtain f′(t)×g(t)=|ijk104t3t2t3t|=|04t3t3t|i−|14t3t2t|j+|10t2t3|k=⟨−4t6,4t5−t,t3⟩,f(t)×g′(t)=|ijkt5t42t3t21|=|5t43t21|i−|tt42t1|j+|t52t3t2|k=⟨5−3t6,2t5−t,3t3−10t⟩.

Finally,

(f×g)′(t)=⟨−4t6,4t5−t,t3⟩+⟨5−3t6,2t5−t,3t3−10t⟩=⟨−7t6+5,6t5−2t,4t3−10t⟩.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms (f×g)'=f'×g+f×g'. Adding ⟨−4t⁶,4t⁵−t,t³⟩ and ⟨5−3t⁶,2t⁵−t,3t³−10t⟩ gives ⟨−7t⁶+5,6t⁵−2t,4t³−10t⟩, exactly option d. The deliberately submitted option b is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Using the Product Rules for Differentiation
content.worked_solution:
Using the cross product rule, we can write:

$$
(f\times g)^{′}(t)={f}^{′}(t)\times g(t)+f(t)\times {g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,4{t}^{3}⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,3{t}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t)\times g(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{2} & {t}^{3} & t\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{3} & t\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{2} & t\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ {t}^{2} & {t}^{3}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =⟨-4{t}^{6},\,4{t}^{5}-t,\,{t}^{3}⟩, \\ f(t)\times {g}^{′}(t) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ t & 5 & {t}^{4} \\ 2t & 3{t}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & {t}^{4} \\ 3{t}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}t & {t}^{4} \\ 2t & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}t & 5 \\ 2t & 3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}|k \\  & =⟨5-3{t}^{6},\,2{t}^{5}-t,\,3{t}^{3}-10t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}(f\times g)^{′}(t) & =⟨-4{t}^{6},\,4{t}^{5}-t,\,{t}^{3}⟩+⟨5-3{t}^{6},\,2{t}^{5}-t,\,3{t}^{3}-10t⟩ \\  & =⟨-7{t}^{6}+5,\,6{t}^{5}-2t,\,4{t}^{3}-10t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the dot product rule, we can write:

$$
({f}^{′}\cdot f)^{′}(t)={f}^{″}(t)\cdot f(t)+{f}^{′}(t)\cdot {f}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the first and second derivative of the function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+2t\,j+4\cdot 2t\,k \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+2t\,j+8t\,k \\ {f}^{″}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8t)\,k \\  & =3\cdot 2t\,i+2j+8\,k \\  & =6t\,i+2j+8\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{′}\cdot f)^{′}(0) & ={f}^{″}(0)\cdot f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)\cdot {f}^{′}(0) \\  & =(6(0)\,i+2\,j+8\,k)\cdot (({0}^{3}-1)\,i+({0}^{2}-2)\,j+4(0)^{2}\,k)+(3(0)^{2}\,i+2(0)\,j+8(0)\,k)\cdot (3(0)^{2}\,i+2(0)\,j+8(0)\,k) \\  & =(2\,j+8\,k)\cdot (-i-2\,j) \\  & =0(-1)+2(-2)+(0) \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$
